import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 550

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/550](https://www.erdosproblems.com/550)
- [Ch77] Chvátal, V., Tree-complete graph Ramsey numbers. J. Graph Theory (1977), 93.
-/

open Filter

namespace Erdos550

/--
Let $m_1\leq\cdots\leq m_k$ and $n$ be sufficiently large. If $T$ is a tree on $n$ vertices
and $G$ is the complete multipartite graph with vertex class sizes $m_1,\ldots,m_k$ then prove that
$$R(T,G)\leq (\chi(G)-1)(R(T,K_{m_1,m_2})-1)+m_1.$$

This problem is #16 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_550 :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (m : Fin k → ℕ) (hm : Monotone m)
      (hm_pos : ∀ i, 0 < m i),
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
        ∀ (T : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), T.IsTree →
          SimpleGraph.graphRamsey T
            (SimpleGraph.completeMultipartiteGraph (fun i ↦ Fin (m i))) ≤
            (k - 1) * (SimpleGraph.graphRamsey T
              (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin (m ⟨0, by omega⟩)) (Fin (m ⟨1, by omega⟩))) - 1) +
                m ⟨0, by omega⟩ := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos550

reformulations.difference: Lean replaces the source's chromatic-number coefficient χ(G)−1 by k−1 and expresses sufficiently large n using ∀ᶠ n in atTop, after fixing the part sizes.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: All parts are nonempty by hm_pos. Coloring vertices by their part gives a k-coloring, while choosing one vertex from each part gives a k-clique, so χ(G)=k. On ℕ, eventual truth at atTop is exactly ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N. The quantifier placement makes N depend on k and the fixed part sizes and makes it uniform over all n-vertex trees, as in the original conjecture. A sorry-free proof of the equivalence with the explicit-threshold, chromatic-number formulation is in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean (Review550.source_equivalence).

sources_consulted: Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp, Multipartite graph–tree Ramsey numbers, Ann. New York Acad. Sci. 576 (1989), 146–154, especially question (2), p. 153: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1989-12.pdf
Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp, Multipartite graph–sparse graph Ramsey numbers, Combinatorica 5 (1985), 311–318, introduction and concluding questions: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1985-15.pdf
https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html (bibliographic entries for the relevant papers)

Chvátal, Tree-complete graph Ramsey numbers, J. Graph Theory 1 (1977), 93, DOI 10.1002/jgt.3190010118; publisher-supplied abstract read at https://api.crossref.org/works?query.title=Tree-complete%20graph%20Ramsey%20numbers&rows=2

E. Li, A Resolution of Erdős Problem 550 on Tree versus Complete Multipartite Ramsey Numbers, arXiv:2606.23659, abstract, introductory statement and main theorem; LaTeX source from https://arxiv.org/e-print/2606.23659
https://users.encs.concordia.ca/~chvatal/ (used to locate the author's bibliography)
review.notes: Checked the sole declaration, its dependent graph definitions, and the quantifiers and arithmetic. graphRamsey uses ordinary injective subgraph copies, not induced copies. Finite Ramsey theory makes its defining set nonempty; both target graphs are nonempty when T.IsTree holds, so the Ramsey-number subtraction does not introduce an unintended truncated value. Lean checks covered multipartite/bipartite adjacency and cardinalities, absence of an empty tree, existence of trees at every positive order, the singleton Ramsey number, satisfiability of the part-size hypotheses, and the elementary k=2 boundary. The source still records OPEN and lists Li's paper only as a claimed resolution, so there is no status discrepancy. Wiley blocked the full Chvátal article; its quoted background theorem was checked against the publisher-supplied abstract. The reviewed file remains unchanged.
